ideas.title: MI-RR: retrieve-and-rerank mutual-information kNN graphs and certified metric sketching for million-cell clustering
ideas.one_line: Make MICA's exact MI geometry work at 2M+ cells by treating kNN graph construction as a retrieval problem: cheap candidate generators, exact GPU MI reranking, and a sketch in MI space with a coverage certificate. Then test whether MI actually helps at atlas scale.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
1) Scale. MICA-GE is the only MI-distance clustering method that runs at scale. The largest published run is Covid650K (647,366 cells): 13 h and 204 GB on 40 CPU cores, with no GPU path and no accuracy check above about 14K labeled cells (Pan et al., Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6, Supp. Fig. 4 and Source Data).
2) Code as it stands. I checked `main` on 2026-09-16. `MICA/mica_ge.py` builds the MI kNN graph with a custom `hnswlib.Index(space='mi')` fork. `lib/neighbor_graph.py build_graph` calls `kneighbors_graph(mode='distance')` and then `.toarray()`. That dense n x n matrix would be about 32 TB at 2M cells, and it passes distances as edge weights, so farther neighbors weigh more. A colleague's projection for 2M cells is over 12 h and 450 to 650 GB (estimate).
3) No prior art at this scale. Nobody has built a kNN graph under an MI distance over more than 1M objects in any field (colleague sweep). My arXiv API query abs:"mutual information" AND abs:"nearest neighbor graph" (2026-09-16) returned only MI estimators. Every sketching method uses PCA or Euclidean space: geosketch, Hopper, Seurat v5 leverage sketch.
4) Accuracy at scale is untested. Skinnider et al. (Nat Methods 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0372-4) found MI weak on small data, so the claim that MI helps may not hold at atlas scale.
5) Unused structure. MICA's distance D = 1 - I/H(X,Y) is a proper metric (Vinh, Epps and Bailey, JMLR 2010), so metric-space indexing and k-center guarantees apply. Nobody has used them for cell clustering.
ideas.method_sketch:
1) Sparse exact MI kernel.
- Compute MICA's per-cell equal-width bin codes once. Store only the nonzero genes as (gene, uint8 bin).
- The joint-histogram cell (0,0) equals G minus the size of the union of the two cells' nonzero genes. This holds when bin 0 contains only zeros, which is typical at 10x depth: one UMI in a 5,000-UMI cell gives log2(CPM+1) of about 7.6, far above the first bin width. Assert this per dataset.
- A Triton/CUDA kernel computes batched exact NVI for (query, candidate) lists. Check it against MICA's numba metric on random pairs.

2) Candidate generation, borrowed from IR, with the union of candidates reranked by exact MI:
- (a) PCA-cosine ANN with FAISS or cuML.
- (b) MinHash/LSH on detected-gene sets (Broder 1997). Jaccard on detection is a proxy for the co-detection term that dominates plug-in MI.
- (c) Landmark/CUR: exact MI to m anchor cells, as ANNCUR and ADACUR do for cross-encoders. Add triangle-inequality lower bounds |D(x,l) - D(y,l)| <= D(x,y) for exact pruning.
- An adaptive second round, as in ADACUR, handles queries whose bound-based coverage is low.

3) Metric sketch.
- Farthest-first traversal under NVI on GPU (the k-center 2-approximation that Hopper uses in Euclidean space).
- Certificate: the covering radius eps_s is known exactly once sketching ends. Any population whose MI gap to all other cells exceeds eps_s must contain a sketch point, and 1-NN propagation labels its cells correctly.
- Report which reference rare types are certified.

4) Clustering.
- Run Leiden (CPM and modularity) directly on the reranked MI kNN graph, with similarity weights 1 - D.
- Ablate against MICA's chain: node2vec, Euclidean kNN, Louvain.
- Sketch mode: build the exact MI graph on the sketch, then propagate labels by MI-kNN vote.

5) Deliverable. A drop-in GPU backend for `mica ge` with modern dependencies (MICA currently pins anndata 0.8.0, networkx<3 and Python 3.9).
ideas.experiments:
Datasets by regime
- D2 (>=2M x >=10): Allen whole mouse brain 10Xv3, 2.3M cells x 32,285 genes, with class, subclass, supertype and cluster labels (CC BY-NC, public S3; Yao et al., Nature 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06812-z). For labels that are not circular, add a 2M-cell slice of Tahoe-100M (CC0, cell-line labels by demuxlet; https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.02.20.639398).
- D1 (>=5,000 x >=20): PBMC14K (13,605 x 17,986, FACS labels; scMINER's own anchor dataset).
  - If the instructor requires low-dimensional data, use Levine_32dim CyTOF (265,627 x 32; HDCytoData). Report it honestly: MI between cells over 32 features is degenerate (b = 3 bins). Optionally add an exploratory variant that takes MI between cells' distance profiles to 1,000 landmarks.
- D3 (>=500 x >=700):
  - Zeisel 2015 (3,005 x 19,972)
  - CellBench 10x (3,803 x 11,778, genotype labels; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0425-8)
  - Chu 2016 (1,018 x 19,097)
  - These small sets allow brute-force exact MI, which validates kernel exactness and recall.

Retrieval evaluation
- recall@k against exact brute-force MI kNN on 50K to 100K random subsamples of D2.
- Recall versus number of MI evaluations, for each candidate generator.
- Intrinsic dimensionality rho = mu^2 / (2 sigma^2) (Chavez et al., ACM Comput Surv 2001), to predict how much pruning can help.

Clustering evaluation
- ARI, AMI and NMI at each hierarchy level.
- Hierarchy-weighted wNMI (Wu and Wu, Genome Biol 2020, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02027-x).
- F1 on rare supertypes (<0.1% of cells) and the fraction of rare types the sketch certifies.
- Wall time and peak RAM/VRAM.
- Report both oracle k (comparable to scMINER) and a label-free resolution.

Baselines
- MICA-GE on CPU, up to the largest feasible size (about 100K to 300K cells)
- rapids-singlecell PCA + Leiden
- Scanpy on CPU
- Seurat v5 sketch + ProjectData
- SC3s
- geosketch or Hopper in PCA space + kNN propagation
- minicore JSD k-means

Ablations
- Candidate generator
- k_cand in {50, 100, 300}
- All genes vs HVGs
- node2vec on/off
- Distance vs similarity edge weights
- Sketch size
- Farthest-first vs uniform vs leverage sampling
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are rough and must be profiled in week 2.
- Data loading: the Allen 10Xv3 raw h5ad files total about 95 GB. As sparse CSR with int64 indices the matrix is about 84 GB, which fits in 754 GB of RAM.
- Exact brute-force MI on 50K cells: 1.25e9 pairs at about 5K to 6K operations per pair, roughly 7e12 operations. Estimate 1 to 3 GPU-hours on 2x RTX 6000 Ada.
- Reranking 2.3M cells x 300 candidates (7e8 pairs): estimate 0.5 to 2 GPU-hours.
- Candidate generation: FAISS or cuML ANN in minutes. MinHash on CPU in under 1 h.
- Farthest-first sketch of 5K to 20K centers, on HVG-restricted 4-bit codes: estimate 1 to 5 GPU-hours.
- Leiden with cuGraph: minutes.
- The full pipeline is designed to fit inside one 12 h window. The MICA-GE CPU baseline is capped by cell count (Covid97K took 1.3 h on 40 cores).
- No model training.

- The dataset documentation the course requires for all three regimes: source, variables, preprocessing, label provenance and label trust tier.

Shared: the certificate argument is a one-page proof suited to a joint writing session.
ideas.novelty_claim:
A reviewer would check four claims.
1) This is the first MI-distance kNN graph and clustering at >=2M cells, with kNN recall measured against exact MI.
2) It is the first use of retrieve-and-rerank (cheap proxy candidates, exact expensive metric) and CUR/landmark lower-bound pruning to build single-cell kNN graphs under a non-Euclidean information metric.
3) It is the first sketch in NVI geometry with a per-population coverage and propagation certificate.
4) It is the first accuracy benchmark of MI-based clustering at atlas scale with hierarchical and rare-type metrics. It answers whether scMINER's small-data advantage (mean ARI 0.844 vs Seurat 0.733 on 10 datasets, oracle k) survives at scale.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
Base method
- MICA/scMINER (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6; code https://github.com/jyyulab/MICA, `mica_ge.py` and `lib/neighbor_graph.py`, checked 2026-09-16).

Information-theoretic clustering at scale
- minicore, which runs divergence k-means on 4M cells (Baker et al., bioRxiv 2021, https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859).

Sketching
- Hopper, farthest-first sketching (DeMeo and Berger, Bioinformatics 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa408).
- geosketch (Hie et al., Cell Systems 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2019.05.003).
- Seurat v5 sketch (Hao et al., Nat Biotechnol 2024, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01767-y).

kNN search under expensive similarities
- CUR-based kNN search for cross-encoders:
  - ANNCUR, arXiv 2210.12579 (2022; EMNLP 2022 venue from memory, UNVERIFIED)
  - ADACUR, arXiv 2305.02996 (2023; Findings of ACL venue UNVERIFIED)
  - Yadav et al., arXiv 2405.03651 (2024; the arXiv abstract listing says ICLR 2024)
- MinHash (Broder 1997, https://doi.org/10.1109/SEQUEN.1997.666900).
- Metric-space search survey (Chavez et al., ACM Comput Surv 2001, https://doi.org/10.1145/502807.502808).
- NVI is a metric (Vinh et al., JMLR 2010, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf).
- Learned embeddings that approximate an expensive metric (Courty et al., ICLR 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07457).

GPU pipelines and atlas practice
- rapids-singlecell (arXiv 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02402).
- Allen atlas cluster-then-propagate (Yao et al., Nature 2023).
ideas.risks:
Scientific risks
- MI may not beat PCA + Leiden at scale. The result would then be a benchmark plus a tool: a lower venue, but still a solid course project.
- NVI distances may concentrate, so triangle-inequality pruning may not help. The candidate generators may miss MI neighbors. Both are measurable by week 3.
- Allen labels come from clustering in PCA/Jaccard-Leiden space, which biases the comparison against MI. Add the Tahoe slice for non-circular labels.

Engineering risks
- Reviewers may call this engineering. The recall analysis, certificate and atlas-scale accuracy have to carry the paper, and the certificate itself is simple.
- Irregular sparse GPU kernels can underperform. Fallback: dense 4-bit codes on 3K to 5K HVGs.

Competition
- The Yu lab has open sparse branches (`huge_dataset`, PR #30) and migrated its repos in 2026-07. They could release a faster version.

Plan
- Go/no-go in mid October 2026: recall@20 >= 0.9 with <= 300 candidates on a 50K-cell subsample.
- Recommendation: rank 1 for the course (it naturally covers all three regimes and fits Utshab's skills). Pair it with idea 2's cheap week-1 depth diagnostic.
ideas.venue_ideas:
- Bioinformatics (original paper), or the ISMB 2027 proceedings track (typically a January deadline; UNVERIFIED).
- RECOMB 2027, only if results are ready by its autumn deadline (UNVERIFIED).
- ACM BCB 2027.
- A method-general IR framing (retrieve-and-rerank kNN graph construction under expensive metrics) could go to the KDD 2027 applied data science track or as a SIGIR 2027 short paper (deadlines UNVERIFIED).
- Course: the centerpiece for the large-scale clustering regime.

ideas.title: Depth-calibrated information distance: correcting what cell-cell mutual information measures in sparse counts
ideas.one_line: Test whether MICA's plug-in cell-cell MI mostly encodes sequencing depth and co-detection. Then build a null-calibrated, chance-adjusted information distance that is depth-invariant by construction and plugs into MICA.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
1) The estimator. I checked `MICA/lib/distance.py` on `main` (2026-09-16).
- Equal-width bins are computed separately for each cell, between that cell's own min and max. b = floor(G^(1/3)).
- MI is a plug-in estimate from the 2D histogram, with no bias correction. Zeros share bin 0.
- The returned distance is 1 - I/H(X,Y).

2) The depth mechanism (my derivation, not yet measured).
- After log2(CPM+1), one UMI maps to 8.97 in a 2,000-UMI cell but to 5.67 in a 20,000-UMI cell.
- With a per-cell max near 15.6 and b = 26 (bin width about 0.6), three things shift with depth: the first occupied nonzero bin, the number of empty bins, and the zero-bin mass.
- D(i,j) is therefore plausibly a function of the two depths and detection rates, not only of cell state.

3) What has not been tested.
- scMINER only varied the bin count (5 to 100) on small sets.
- A Europe PMC query ("mutual information" AND (sequencing depth OR library size) AND cell-cell, 2019 to 2026; run 2026-09-16) found no study of depth invariance in cell-cell MI.
- PBMC14K sorted populations were separate libraries, so depth lines up with labels. Part of MICA's PBMC14K advantage (ARI 0.853) could be depth signal. Untested.

4) What exists.
- Count-aware MI estimators are all gene-gene:
  - Mixed KSG (Gao et al., NeurIPS 2017)
  - Normi (Brief Bioinform 2023)
  - MIMIQ (bioRxiv 2026)
- Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber (Nat Methods 2023) built a downsampling kNN-overlap benchmark for transformations, but did not include MI.
- Skinnider 2019 found MI weak, possibly because of the estimator.
ideas.method_sketch:
1) Diagnose.
- Binomially thin single cells to 50%, 25% and 10% depth. Measure D(i, thinned i), the change in each cell's kNN set, and the partial correlation of D with |log s_i - log s_j| within true types.
- Split plug-in MI with the chain rule into a co-detection term I(Z_i; Z_j) on binary detection and a magnitude term over co-detected genes.

2) Estimator family (DCID).
(a) Depth-robust discretization. Bin per-gene analytic Pearson residuals (Lause et al. 2021) or per-gene ranks (copula), with zero as its own symbol.
(b) Null correction, analogous to how modularity subtracts a degree-preserving null.
- E0[I | s_i, s_j] is the expected MI for two cells drawn from one homogeneous Poisson or NB population with global gene means mu_g and depths s_i, s_j.
- Tabulate it by Monte Carlo on a 30x30 grid of depth quantiles and interpolate.
- Define D* = 1 - (I - E0) / (H_ref - E0), in the style of AMI (Vinh et al., ICML 2009).
(c) Finite-sample shrinkage. James-Stein entropy and MI (Hausser and Strimmer, JMLR 2009), for the low-feature regime.
(d) Optionally, separate null-corrected weights for the two chain-rule terms.

3) Integration.
- Drop-in replacement for MICA's metric in MDS mode and in GE mode (or in idea 1's kernel).
- D* is not guaranteed to be a metric. Report the rate of triangle-inequality violations, and apply a simple metric repair if needed.

4) Theory.
- Show that E[D*] is invariant to depth under the homogeneous null, by construction.
- Derive the bias of plug-in MI as a function of zero fraction and b.
ideas.experiments:
Datasets by regime
- D3 (>=500 x >=700):
  - Zeisel (3,005 x 19,972)
  - Chu 2016 (1,018 x 19,097; labels from experimental design)
  - CellBench 10x and CEL-seq2 (genotype labels; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0425-8)
  - Kolodziejczyk (704 cells)
  - A deeply sequenced full-length dataset for the downsampling benchmark, reusing the Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber setup (exact dataset UNVERIFIED).
- D1 (>=5,000 x >=20):
  - PBMC14K (13,605 x 17,986). Equalize depth across the sorted libraries by thinning, then recluster. If ARI drops, depth was contributing.
  - Levine_32dim CyTOF (265,627 x 32), used only as a low-feature stress test for the shrinkage estimator (c). CyTOF has no depth.
- D2 (>=2M x >=10): Allen WMB 10Xv3 (2.3M x 32K), or a 2M-cell slice of Allen MERFISH (4.3M x 550 genes), where cell volume creates depth-like variation. Take a 200K geosketch, build an MI kNN graph per estimator, run Leiden, and propagate labels by kNN to all cells. Score with hierarchical metrics.

Baselines
- MICA default (NVI) and its 1 - I/sqrt(Hx Hy) code variant
- Pearson and Spearman on log-CPM
- Proportionality rho_p (best in Skinnider 2019)
- log1p + PCA + Leiden (the winner in Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber)
- Analytic Pearson residuals + PCA
- GLM-PCA
- Mixed KSG on 1K to 2K-cell subsets

Metrics
- kNN overlap with the deep reference after downsampling.
- Within-type correlation of distance with depth difference.
- ARI, AMI and NMI at oracle k and at a label-free resolution.
- Rare-type F1.

Ablations
- Each of (a) to (d) on its own and combined.
- Binning rule.
- All genes vs HVGs.
- Poisson vs NB null.
- Null grid resolution.
ideas.compute_estimate:
Small.
- Full MI matrices for up to 15K cells are at most 1.1e8 pairs: minutes on one GPU, or a few hours with numba on 120 cores.
- The null table needs about 1e5 to 1e6 MI evaluations: seconds to minutes.
- Thinning replicates (10 per setting) multiply this only modestly.
- D2 sketch path: a 200K-cell MI kNN graph takes a few GPU-hours with idea 1's kernel, or roughly 3 to 6 h on CPU with MICA's HNSW (estimate from Covid97K taking 1.3 h on 40 cores).
- Whole project well under a few GPU-days. No training.

ideas.novelty_claim:
A reviewer would check three claims.
1) This is the first quantification of depth and detection confounding in MI distance between cells, as opposed to between genes.
2) It is the first chance- and null-corrected information distance between cells, using a configuration-model-style null over depth that makes it depth-invariant by construction.
3) It is the first head-to-head comparison of MI estimators for cell-cell distance on a downsampling kNN-overlap benchmark, next to the standard transformations.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
Base method
- MICA estimator (https://github.com/jyyulab/MICA/blob/main/MICA/lib/distance.py; paper https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6).

Similarity and transformation benchmarks
- Skinnider et al., Nat Methods 2019 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0372-4).
- Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber, Nat Methods 2023, 20:665 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01814-1).
- Analytic Pearson residuals (Lause, Berens, Kobak, Genome Biol 2021, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02451-7).

Chance correction and shrinkage
- AMI and correction for chance (Vinh et al., ICML 2009, https://doi.org/10.1145/1553374.1553511; JMLR 2010).
- James-Stein entropy (Hausser and Strimmer, JMLR 2009, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v10/hausser09a.html).

Count-aware MI estimators (all gene-gene)
- Mixed discrete-continuous KSG (Gao et al., NeurIPS 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06212).
- Normi (Brief Bioinform 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbad326).
- MIMIQ (bioRxiv 2026, https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.10.717770).

Same lab
- The Yu lab's transcriptome-size normalization (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56623-1). Must be read, since it overlaps in spirit.
ideas.risks:
Premise risk
- The premise may fail: per-cell CPM plus all-gene binning might already be robust to depth. The thinning diagnostic takes 1 to 2 weeks and serves as the go/no-go.

Outcome risks
- log1p + PCA may still win overall (as in Ahlmann-Eltze and Huber), giving a mixed result that needs careful framing (for example, gains on depth-heterogeneous data only).
- On PBMC14K the corrected distance could lower ARI because depth aligns with labels. That is a real finding, but it looks bad on the anchor dataset.

Method risks
- D* is not guaranteed to be a metric, which conflicts with idea 1's pruning and certificate.
- A null built from global gene means mixes cell types. Analytic Pearson residuals have the same issue, and reviewers will ask about it.
- The Yu lab's transcriptome-size normalization may already address part of this.

Recommendation: rank 2. The week-1 diagnostic is cheap and informs ideas 1 and 3 whichever way it comes out.

ideas.title: Leakage-free network-activity clustering: auditing and cross-fitting scMINER's driver-activity space
ideas.one_line: Check whether scMINER's activity-based clustering accuracy is partly built in by construction (per-group networks plus group-specific missing-value filling). Then propose a cross-fitted, all-network activity representation and a co-refinement clustering whose accuracy cannot leak labels.
ideas.method_sketch:
1) Leakage audit with negative controls.
(a) Random groups. Assign cells uniformly at random to K groups, build per-group networks, score with `getActivity_inBatch`, and cluster. Without leakage, ARI to the random groups should be about 0.
(b) Nuisance groups. Repeat with depth quartiles or donor as the groups.
(c) Label swap. Score each group's cells with another group's network.
(d) Fill ablation. Compare min fill, zero fill and a union-target universe.

2) Leakage-free representation.
- Score every cell under every group network (network-projection features, in the spirit of metaVIPER).
- Use one shared driver universe, and treat missing edges as absent targets instead of group-specific constants.

3) Cross-fitting.
- Split cells into folds. Learn clusters and networks on fold A, then compute activity features and cluster the fold-B cells. Swap the folds.
- Align labels across folds with Hungarian matching on network-projection profiles.

4) Co-refinement clustering.
- Iterate: cluster, cross-fitted networks, activity of all cells under all networks, recluster (MICA or Leiden).
- Stop when the ARI between iterations exceeds 0.95, with an iteration cap. This is an EM-like mixture of regulatory programs. Compare it with the one-shot pipeline.

5) Keep network inference light.
- Run SJARACNe on metacells with fewer bootstraps, or a GPU gene-gene MI with DPI pruning.
- Use prior networks (CollecTRI/DoRothEA via decoupleR) as a leakage-free reference.

6) Optional module for the team's RAG motivation.
- Use the cross-fitted hidden drivers of each cluster as retrieval queries over PubMed and marker evidence, with a local model served by vLLM.
- No LLM annotation method uses computed TF or driver activity as evidence (colleague sweep).
- Keep this separate from the clustering claim.
ideas.experiments:
Datasets by regime
- D1 (>=5,000 x >=20):
  - PBMC14K (13,605 x 17,986; 7 FACS types). A direct re-test of ARI 0.87.
  - Hao 2021 CITE-seq PBMC (about 162K cells, 228 ADT proteins; count UNVERIFIED; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.048). Surface proteins give an orthogonal check of activity for drivers measured as protein.
- D3 (>=500 x >=700):
  - scMINER's Treg tissue dataset (Spleen, Lung, Skin, VAT), a re-test of ARI 0.998. Its accession and size are UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed to meet the thresholds.
  - Zeisel (3,005 x 19,972) and Chu 2016 (1,018 x 19,097) as standard sets.
- D2 (>=2M x >=10): a 2M-cell slice of Parse 10M PBMC cytokines (18 cell types plus 90 cytokine conditions; CC BY-NC) or of Tahoe-100M (CC0; cell line plus drug).
  - Build networks on a sketch or metacells.
  - Score all 2M cells by sparse drivers x genes times genes x cells products on GPU, then run GPU Leiden in activity space.
  - Repeat the random-group audit at this scale.

Baselines
- scMINER default activity clustering
- MICA on expression
- SCENIC AUCell with pooled regulons
- metaVIPER/PISCES-style scoring via pyVIPER (BMC Bioinformatics 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-026-06524-x)
- decoupleR with CollecTRI priors
- Scanpy/Seurat Leiden on expression

Metrics
- ARI and AMI against truth.
- Leakage index: ARI to random or nuisance groups.
- Accuracy drop under label swap.
- Cross-fold consistency.
- Spearman correlation between CITE-seq protein and activity.
- On D2: separation of cytokine or drug conditions that expression-based clustering misses.

Ablations
- Fill rule
- Per-group vs all-network scoring
- Cross-fitting on/off
- Bootstrap count
- Metacell gamma
- Number of co-refinement iterations
ideas.compute_estimate:
Network inference dominates the cost.
- SJARACNe's cost is poorly documented. The PBMC14K demo reserves 8 GB. A 2025 comment on SJARACNe issue #50 reports 160 to 200 GB for 1,361 cells on 32 cores.
- Plan: 1,000 cells or metacells per group, 20 to 30 bootstraps for the audits, groups run in parallel on 120 cores.
- Rough estimate: 1 to 4 CPU-hours per group (UNVERIFIED). The audit design needs about 40 to 60 network builds, so several 12-hour windows.
- Fallback that cuts this sharply: prior networks, or GPU gene-gene MI.
- Activity scoring for 2M cells is a sparse matrix product on GPU and takes minutes. GPU Leiden takes minutes.
- Optional LLM: Qwen3-32B in BF16 split across the two GPUs with vLLM, inference only.
- No training.

- CITE-seq protein vs activity comparisons.

Utshab

ideas.novelty_claim:
A reviewer would check three claims.
1) This is the first quantitative leakage audit, with negative controls, of clustering in network-activity space built from per-group networks (scMINER, and by extension PISCES-style pipelines). If confirmed, it shows that published activity-clustering ARIs are inflated by construction.
2) It introduces a cross-fitted, all-network activity representation and an iterative co-refinement clustering whose accuracy cannot come from label leakage.
3) Optionally, it is the first use of computed driver activity, rather than marker genes, as retrieval evidence for cluster interpretation.

ideas.risks:
Finding risks
- The per-cell-type networks may have been built on MICA clusters rather than true labels. The headline inflation claim would then weaken, though the audit and the self-reinforcement result would still stand.
- Leakage may be small if most drivers appear in every group's network, so that the min fill rarely applies. Measure the NA fraction in week 1 as the go/no-go.

Professional risk
- Critiquing a recent Nature Communications paper needs care. Share the audit with the authors before posting, and consider the Matters Arising route.

Practical risks
- SJARACNe installation and memory failures are well documented (issues #44, #50 to #57). Fall back to prior networks or GPU MI.
- Reviewers may see co-refinement as incremental over PISCES. The audit has to carry the paper.
- The RAG module is in a crowded area and must not dominate the clustering story.

Recommendation: rank 3 for a paper, but the fastest route to a striking, easily explained result, and the best vehicle for the non-CS teammates and the original RAG motivation.

ideas.title: Thinning-validated merging: label-free resolution selection for MI-distance clustering that stays valid despite double dipping
ideas.one_line: Replace scMINER's oracle k with a count-thinning merge test that works with any cell-cell distance, including MI. Depth-stratified permutations keep depth gradients from passing as real splits.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
1) Oracle k. scMINER's headline accuracy either gives MDS mode the true k or sweeps GE resolution until the cluster count matches the truth.
- On Zeisel, GE-mode ARI ranges from about 0.12 to 0.81 across resolutions.
- The docs pick PBMC14K resolution 2.05 from prior knowledge, and the authors call choosing K manual and problem-dependent.

2) Calibrated methods do not cover this case. CHOIR (Nat Genet 2025), sc-SHC (Nat Methods 2023) and recall (AJHG 2025) assume PCA or gene-count features, not an arbitrary cell-cell distance, and none has been applied to MI clustering.

3) Stability is not validity. scICE, chooseR and MultiK measure stability, and stable splits can still come from noise or depth.

4) Double dipping. Testing splits on the same counts that produced them inflates significance (Neufeld et al., Biostatistics). Count splitting has been used to choose K for k-means and latent-variable models, not to test merges of graph-based clusters under a non-Euclidean metric.
- My Europe PMC and arXiv API queries on data thinning or count splitting plus clustering (2026-09-16) found no merge test for Leiden or Louvain clusters.
- The closest hits are generalized data thinning (JASA 2025) and a comment on data fission for post-clustering inference (JASA 2025).

5) The depth trap. Thinning makes train and test noise independent. But a split made along a depth gradient in the training fold persists in the test fold, so a naive test will confirm technical splits. I found no method that handles this for merge testing (CHOIR internals UNVERIFIED on this point).
ideas.method_sketch:
1) Split the data.
- Counts: split X = X_tr + X_te by Poisson thinning (epsilon = 0.5), or NB thinning with estimated overdispersion (Neufeld et al., arXiv 2307.12985).
- Continuous CyTOF: Gaussian data fission on arcsinh values with an estimated noise scale (Leiner et al., arXiv 2112.11079). Fall back to splitting cells.

2) Over-cluster X_tr with MICA: MDS + k-means at large k, or MI kNN + Leiden at high resolution. Build a merge tree by average linkage of clusters in MI distance, or from the resolution path as in MRtree.

3) Test each sibling pair on X_te only.
- Use metric-space two-sample statistics computed from MI distances among at most 300 + 300 subsampled cells: the Friedman-Rafsky cross-match count on the pooled MI kNN graph, or energy distance.
- Permutation null, with permutations stratified by depth decile so exchangeability respects depth.
- Optionally use idea 2's depth-calibrated distance.

4) Test top-down with FWER control (as in sc-SHC) and merge pairs that are not significant. Output:
- the selected k;
- a p-value for each cluster;
- a certified partition that downstream differential activity and hidden-driver analysis can use without double dipping.

5) Aggregate p-values over several thinning draws (for example 5, with Cauchy combination) to reduce split randomness.

6) Scale. Tests use only subsamples, so the cost is O(tree nodes x 600^2) and does not depend on n. For 2M cells, over-cluster a sketch, test, then propagate labels.
ideas.experiments:
Calibration under the null
- Data: homogeneous populations, such as a single CellBench cell line, single-line 10x datasets (for example Jurkat or 293T; availability details UNVERIFIED), and scDesign3 or Splatter one-population simulations with a realistic spread of depths.
- Metrics: false split rate (selected k > 1) and QQ plots of p-values.

Power, by regime
- D3 (>=500 x >=700):
  - CellBench 10x (5 cell lines, 3,803 x 11,778) and its RNA-mixture design
  - Chu 2016 (1,018 x 19,097)
  - Kolodziejczyk (704 cells, 3 culture conditions)
  - Zeisel at two label levels (9 classes and 47 subclasses)
- D1 (>=5,000 x >=20):
  - Levine_32dim CyTOF (265,627 x 32, 14 gated populations), using data fission with Euclidean distance on arcsinh values. This shows the test works with any metric.
  - PBMC14K with MI distance.
- D2 (>=2M x >=10): a 2M-cell slice of Tahoe-100M (CC0, 50 cell lines, demuxlet labels) or Allen WMB 2.3M. Check which level of the label hierarchy the selected k lands on.

Baselines
- MICA with oracle k (upper bound)
- MICA with k chosen by silhouette (the authors' suggestion)
- Leiden at default resolution
- CHOIR, including CHOIR run on MICA's MDS coordinates
- sc-SHC `testClusters` applied to MICA labels
- recall
- scICE
- chooseR
- MultiK
- The same test without thinning, to measure how much double dipping inflates significance

Metrics
- |selected k - k| at each hierarchy level
- ARI and AMI at the selected k
- wNMI (Wu and Wu 2020)
- Rare-type F1
- False split rate on null data
- Runtime

Ablations
- epsilon
- Poisson vs NB thinning
- Cross-match vs energy statistic
- Depth stratification on/off
- Number of thinning draws
- MI vs PCA-Euclidean distance inside the same test
ideas.compute_estimate:
Mostly CPU.
- Each test uses at most 3.6e5 distance pairs, and permutations reuse the same distance matrix.
- A few hundred tests per dataset take minutes to about an hour on 120 cores.
- Null simulations take CPU-hours.
- A 2M-cell run (sketch clustering, tests, propagation) takes a few hours, or less using idea 1's GPU kernel.
- CHOIR says it costs more than a single Louvain run, so cap that baseline to subsamples at 2M cells.
- No training.

ideas.novelty_claim:
A reviewer would check four claims.
1) This is the first merge and resolution test that stays valid after clustering, through count thinning or data fission.
2) It is the first such test that accepts any cell-cell distance, including MI. That removes scMINER's reliance on oracle k.
3) It is the first to guard explicitly against depth-driven false splits, using depth-stratified permutations.
4) It gives the first measurement of how much double dipping inflates split significance for graph-based single-cell clustering.

ideas.risks:
Novelty risks
- This is the most crowded of the four areas (CHOIR, sc-SHC, recall). Reviewers will ask why not simply run CHOIR on MICA's MDS coordinates. The paper must include that baseline and win on null calibration or on MI-specific structure.
- Most of the theory is borrowed. The contribution is the combination (any metric, thinning, depth stratification) plus the evaluation.

Statistical risks
- Poisson thinning is invalid under overdispersion, and NB thinning needs a known dispersion.
- Halving counts reduces power on shallow 10x or sci-RNA data and changes MI geometry, since bin placement moves at half depth (this links to idea 2).
- Depth-stratified permutation may not fully remove depth confounding.
- Data fission for CyTOF depends on an approximate noise model.

Recommendation: rank 4 as a stand-alone paper. It works well as the model-selection module inside idea 1 or 2, and it removes the oracle-k weakness that any reviewer of an scMINER extension will raise.
